fields.weather: Overcast, 52°F. Wind west-southwest about 8 mph. Ground saturated after 0.6 inch of rain overnight.
fields.load: Normal production day: pipe crew laying 48-inch pipe at stations 14+00 to 18+00
fields.staffing: About 70 on site: Larkspur crews plus Pike & Marlow Paving, Hollis Electric and Cascade Dewatering. Superintendent and Safety Director on site.
fields.narration: STARTEX. This is an exercise. It is not a safety evaluation of any real structure. It is 09:45 on Wednesday, April 14, 2027, at the Stillwater Creek Interceptor Phase 2, east of downtown Dayton. The sky is overcast, it is 52 degrees, and the ground is saturated after six-tenths of an inch of rain overnight. About 70 workers are on site. The pipe crew is laying 48-inch pipe in the 13-foot trench at stations 14+00 to 18+00, working from the 10-by-20-foot trench box in Type C soil. Excavator E-7, run by Gordon Pruitt, is digging ahead of the box toward station 16+00. At 06:45, competent person Tomas Reyes signed form LC-F-22 and cleared the trench, with one note: seepage, south wall, station 16+00. In trailer 2, the monitoring display shows the Harlan & Weir print shop crack gauges at CG-1 0.03 inch, CG-2 0.05 inch and CG-3 0.09 inch. The alarm level is 0.12 inch and the action level is 0.25 inch. Site Superintendent Marcus Hale and Safety Director Priya Venkataraman are on site. All operations are normal.
